idiom_name: JUnit @Test with @BeforeEach fixture and AssertJ assertions
implementation_notes: JUnit Jupiter supplies the skeleton - @Test marks the method, @BeforeEach runs the arrange beat before each test and @AfterEach the teardown - while act and assert are ordinary statements in the body; AssertJ's fluent assertThat(...).isEqualTo(...) keeps the assert beat explicit about expected and actual, and its BDDAssertions.then(...) entry point renames the same assertion into the Given-When-Then vocabulary. The classic fixture-class structure survives as @Nested classes with @DisplayName descriptions, and resource lifecycles use @TempDir or @AutoClose; arrange inside the test method whenever only one test needs the state.
pitfalls: @BeforeEach methods are inherited and run outer-first, so a nested test can depend on an enclosing fixture its body never mentions, making the arrange beat invisible to the reader.

The default lifecycle creates a new test class instance per method, so a fixture shared across tests needs @TestInstance(PER_CLASS) (or static state) and must then be thread-safe under parallel execution.

JUnit's assertEquals(expected, actual) boxes primitives and a boolean-only assertion hides the actual value; AssertJ reads the other way round and reports both operands, so mixing the two styles invites inverted expectations.
